title: Billing a Care Level Increase in a Month Already Billed — Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement
content:
**Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement — the level-increase charge.**

### Rule

A care level increase that takes effect inside a month already billed at the earlier level is billed by one level-increase charge on the prorated level change basis, carrying the care level the residency now carries and the span from the first day covered to the last day of that month. The charge is a care fee charge for that billing month and appears on the resident's statement for that month; the amount owed on the residency account goes up by the charge.

A decrease is never billed by the level-increase charge: it takes effect on the first day of the calendar month following the assessment date, and where that day falls inside a month already billed the days at the old level from that day are returned as a level change proration credit referencing the original care fee charge.

Outside the level-increase charge the general billing rules stand: rent and the care level fee are billed in advance on the fee due day of each calendar month for the whole month at the contracted monthly rent and the monthly care fee of the level billed; the move-in month, the month of a rent change and the month in which fees end are prorated by the monthly amount divided by the actual days of that month, multiplied by the days billed counted inclusive of both ends and rounded once to the cent half up; and the care level a resident carries is always the level whose care-point band contains the care points of the most recent assessment.

### Posting the charge

The desk posts the level-increase charge with the agent-side tool `post_level_increase_care_charge_9f33663f`: the tool is first unlocked and then called by the agent. It writes one care fee charge on the prorated level change basis with the values supplied, in the billing month of the first day covered; it does not look anything up or work out the amount.

| Parameter | What it is | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `assisted_residency_id` | Reference number of the assisted living residency charged, as returned by the assisted living residency lookup | Identifier |
| `care_level_billed` | The care level whose increase this charge bills — the care level the residency now carries | One of: Assisted Living Care Level 1, Assisted Living Care Level 2, Assisted Living Care Level 3, Assisted Living Care Level 4, Assisted Living Care Level 5, Assisted Living Care Level 6 |
| `service_from_date` | First day covered by the charge; the billing month of the charge is the month of this day | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `service_to_date` | Last day covered by the charge, in the same month as the first day | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `days_billed` | Number of days covered, counting both the first and the last day | Integer |
| `amount` | The charge in US dollars, positive, already rounded to the cent; it is charged exactly as given | Number with 2 decimal places |

### Return

On success the tool returns `status` "posted", `entry_id` (the reference number of the new care fee charge), `care_level_billed`, `billing_period` (the month charged, YYYY-MM), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places) and `account_balance` (the residency balance in USD after the charge, 2 decimal places). The tool states no error return.

### Points of judgement

| Change found | Billed by the level-increase charge? |
|---|---|
| Increase taking effect inside a month already billed at the earlier level | Yes — one charge for that month |
| Decrease | No — first day of the following month; any days at the old level inside a billed month are returned by a level change proration credit |
